content:
Marissa Cole: Want to sync on launch scope + Console messaging for SCM cost breakdown. Main question: do we label as “Estimated cost” everywhere or only when confidence < 1.0? Also what do we show for assumptions.

Aditya Rao: +1. Optimize is going to consume SCM too, so we should align language. My vote: always “Estimated cost” for v1 to avoid billing confusion.

Nikhil Sharma: Agree. For Hosted users especially, anything that reads like “cost” will get compared to invoice. If we don’t say estimated up front, Support will get hammered.

Henry Cho: From API ergonomics POV: we can expose the field as `estimated_cost` in the payload and Console can render “Estimated cost”. But we should keep it consistent with any docs we publish.

Marissa Cole: Yup. I’m also thinking: top-level label “Estimated cost” + breakdown sections under it (compute/memory/cache etc). Assumptions in a tooltip or expandable panel.

Dylan Brooks: On the UI side, we can do a single label on the page header: “Estimated cost (SCM)” and then the table uses “Cost” columns. If we repeat “estimated” in every row it gets noisy.

Jada Williams: +1 to “Estimated cost” as a header. Then add an info icon “How is this calculated?” linking to assumptions/explain payload fields.

Laura Bennett: Please please keep “estimated” prominent. Also add a line like “Not used for billing” (at least initially). Otherwise we’ll have people treating it as a pricing engine.

Marissa Cole: Ok, messaging proposal v1:
- Header: “Estimated cost”
- Subtext: “Technical estimate based on runtime telemetry and hardware normalization. Not used for billing.”
- Add “Confidence” chip (High/Medium/Low) with tooltip.

Aditya Rao: Works. For Optimize, confidence is a gating signal. If Console shows confidence too, we should match thresholds (e.g., high >= 0.8, medium 0.5–0.8, low < 0.5) unless Eng already decided.

Marissa Cole: I can align to whatever platform ships. But we need copy that makes sense:
- High: “Based on complete telemetry”
- Medium: “Some signals missing; used defaults”
- Low: “Limited telemetry; estimate may be inaccurate”

Nikhil Sharma: Also specify what “missing” means without getting too inside baseball. People don’t know what batch efficiency or KV cache hit rate is.

Henry Cho: Maybe the tooltip text can be slightly more technical, but the default UI should be plain English. We can say “Some runtime signals were unavailable (e.g., caching/batching metrics).”

Dylan Brooks: Implementation note: we’ll have `assumptions[]` and `confidence_score` coming back. For the UI I’d like a stable mapping to 3 buckets so it doesn’t bounce around.

Aditya Rao: Re: assumptions disclosure—Optimize needs the raw assumption list to avoid recommending on top of a pile of defaults. Console should probably surface top 3 assumptions + “View all”.

Marissa Cole: That’s reasonable. I don’t want a wall of text by default.

Elliot Price: From docs side: if we standardize on the exact phrase “Estimated cost” + “Not used for billing”, I can add that to internal docs + a short FAQ for Support. Also define what “confidence” means.

Marissa Cole: Thanks @Elliot. Another open question: do we show $ values or “cost units” for Dedicated/Private where pricing might not be token-based?

Laura Bennett: For SCM it’s “technical cost attribution” so I’d prefer currency only if we’re confident in normalization tables. Otherwise show “$ (estimated)” and keep the caveat.

Aditya Rao: I’d avoid “cost units”. People hate that. If we have a currency output, show it but make assumptions visible. For Private, we can still show estimates because it’s about compute/memory usage; currency might be internal though.

Nikhil Sharma: Careful: Private customers will ask “what is this based on” if we show dollars. Maybe we default to USD internally for Console admin view only? Or show both: “Estimated compute cost” and “Token cost” isn’t a thing there.

Henry Cho: Product decision needed: SCM output schema is likely always currency-like for consistency, but we can gate the UI display. For Private maybe show the breakdown components and hide the top-level $ unless enabled.

Marissa Cole: Let’s keep v1 Console launch scoped to Hosted + Dedicated only. Private later once we validate messaging + telemetry completeness. :thumbsup:

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: That simplifies a lot. Dedicated customers still may compare to contract commits, but that’s less “invoice line item” confusion.

Aditya Rao: Fine by Optimize. We can still use SCM internally for Private experiments; Console doesn’t need to ship it day 1.

Marissa Cole: Great. Final copy tweaks:
- Header: “Estimated cost”
- Helper: “For transparency and optimization. Not used for billing.”
- Confidence tooltip: “Indicates completeness of telemetry used in this estimate.”
- Assumptions section: collapsed by default.

Elliot Price: I’ll draft the FAQ + a snippet Support can paste when customers ask “why does this differ from billing?”

Laura Bennett: Also add a link in the UI: “Learn more about cost estimation” to reduce tickets.

Jada Williams: I’ll create a quick UX note for empty/error state: if SCM is down, show “Cost estimate temporarily unavailable” and don’t show $0.

Marissa Cole: Yes, no $0 ever (we’ve been burned). If estimate missing, show “—” and a tooltip.

Henry Cho: +1. And in API responses we should avoid returning 0 on validation errors; better explicit error code so Console can render the right state.

Aditya Rao: Cool. Next step: I’ll sync with platform on confidence thresholds + exact assumption strings so UI copy doesn’t drift.

Marissa Cole: Sounds good. I’ll update the launch checklist to reflect: Hosted+Dedicated only, “Estimated cost” everywhere, “Not used for billing”, confidence + assumptions disclosure.

Dylan Brooks: I’ll implement the header label + tooltip pattern and will share screenshots in this thread once the component is wired.

Marissa Cole: Thanks all.
